detail: CRITICAL, found while preparing the picks probe. FPLClient._get CACHES 404s (if status_code == 200 or status_code == 404: cache.set) and ResponseCache has NO TTL — get() returns a stored entry forever. cache/fpl_api currently holds 10 picks 404s and 9 entry 404s written pre-deadline on 19-21 Aug. Two distinct harms on the Tue 25 Aug EO sample, the one dataset with no backfill path. (1) sample_picks.py effective_seed defaults to 1_000_000+event_id = deterministic, so draw_uniform_entry_ids reproduces the SAME draw; probe_picks_available reads entry_ids[:10] with no force_refresh, hits the 10 cached 404s, and aborts exit 2 with a message blaming the endpoint or a shape change — sending a debugger at the wrong target while the window closes. If max_id shifts, the draw scatters instead and the 10 become SILENT misses inside the 10,000. (2) WORSE AND SILENT: find_max_valid_entry_id binary-searches via client.entry(id) with no force_refresh, and the 9 cached entry 404s are exactly that search path — Tuesday would replay the entire search FROM CACHE at zero requests and return the max entry id as of 19-21 Aug. The uniform draw would then sample the entry space AS IT WAS BEFORE GW1, systematically excluding every entry created since, at precisely the time FPL player base grows fastest. That is a biased sample frame presented as a uniform one.

Root cause is a category error in the cache policy, not a bug in sample_picks.py. The comment at client.py _get reads cache successes and EXPECTED 404s so a transient 500 does not become sticky — but for entry/ and picks/ a 404 is a TEMPORAL STATE, not a property of the resource. picks/ 404 means not public YET (becomes 200 at the deadline); entry/{id}/ 404 means not issued YET (becomes 200 as the player base grows). Only a genuinely immutable-absent resource may have its 404 cached, and neither of these is one. Fix must be at the client/transport policy layer so no future caller has to remember force_refresh, NOT by sprinkling force_refresh at call sites. Must land before Tue 25 Aug.

CRITICAL, found by the live picks probe — a THIRD API state nobody had modelled. entry/{id}/event/{gw}/picks/ returns HTTP 503 with body The game is being updated. immediately after the deadline. The documented assumption everywhere (client.py entry_picks docstring, sample_picks.py, data-sources.md 2.1) is binary: 404 pre-deadline, 200 after. Reality has a post-deadline MAINTENANCE WINDOW in between. Observed continuously across 8 probe attempts 17:31Z-17:41Z (01:31-01:41 local), every one 503. Three compounding defects: (1) BACKOFF_TRIGGER_STATUSES = (429, 403) EXCLUDES 503, so _get does not back off — it returns immediately and entry_picks raises FPLApiError, since that method models only 404 and 200; (2) 503 is correctly NOT cached (only 200/404 are), so no poisoning from this one; (3) sample_picks.py run() main loop calls client.entry_picks with NO exception handling, so a single 503 anywhere in the 10,000-entry run raises straight out of the loop.

WORST PRE-TUESDAY RISK, compounding the 503 finding: sample_picks.py has NO INCREMENTAL PERSISTENCE. run() accumulates every row into an in-memory all_rows list across the full ~83-minute, 10,000-request sample and only builds/persists the DataFrame AFTER the loop completes. Combined with defect (3) above, a single transient 503 — from an API that demonstrably enters maintenance around gameweek boundaries, which is exactly when this script runs — discards the entire run, every request spent, on the ONE dataset with no backfill path and no second chance (CLAUDE.md, the one irreversible deadline). This is now the top pre-Tuesday item, ABOVE the 404-cache-poisoning finding. Required before Tue 25 Aug: treat 503 as retryable at the transport layer (add to backoff triggers, or model a distinct maintenance state), catch FPLApiError per-entry in the sample loop so one bad response cannot end the run, and persist incrementally so a crash costs the last chunk rather than everything.

Probe patched to treat 503 as not-ready-retry rather than fatal, and a third waiter queued: idle to 18:12Z then 1 request every 5 min for up to 3h (~36 requests total, far inside the 2 req/s ceiling). Snapshotter checked mid-window: last run 01:15 local result 0x0, next 01:45 local — that run falls INSIDE the maintenance window and may fail; a failed ownership snapshot is acceptable and self-healing on the 30-min cadence, but confirm it is not writing a silently stale bootstrap payload.

UNRELATED PRE-EXISTING BUG, found as a side effect of re-running scripts/run_baselines.py to confirm the pinned Phase 1 numbers before/after my migration -- NOT caused by this session's changes (fplai.backtest.* and BitemporalStore.observations()/as_of() are untouched by me). GreedyFormBaseline is genuinely non-deterministic across repeated runs on fully unmodified code: three consecutive runs of scripts/run_baselines.py gave 2020-21 greedy_form totals of 1983, 1991, 1984 (a fourth gave 2003, a fifth 1985); 2021-22 gave 2150 and 2158 across two runs, both ABOVE the brief's pinned upper bound of 2127. random(seed=...) and template are stable across every run (confirmed identical every time). Root cause, traced not guessed: BitemporalStore.observations() (and as_of(), same shape) issues 'SELECT * FROM read_parquet(...) WHERE observed_at <= ?' with NO explicit ORDER BY -- DuckDB does not guarantee output row order for an unordered SELECT. fplai.backtest.baselines.RandomBaseline already carries a defensive comment acknowledging this ('never rely on the store's row order, which is not itself guaranteed stable') and explicitly sorts its element-id list before applying the seeded RNG -- but TemplateBaseline and GreedyFormBaseline build their PlayerCandidate list straight from view.current_attributes/window.group_by output with no equivalent canonicalizing sort, and fplai.backtest.squad.build_squad's hill-climb (squad.py ~line 147 onward) breaks EXACTLY-TIED swap gains by iteration order over that list -- template's ranking values (real ownership counts) essentially never tie exactly so it never hits this path; greedy_form's ranking value (integer trailing-points totals) ties constantly, so it does. I fixed the identical class of bug inside my OWN new store.effective_at() (added a canonical final ORDER BY on the entity key, proven necessary by test_walk_forward_validate_cannot_see_a_folds_own_or_future_outcomes flipping predictions between two builds) but did NOT touch observations()/as_of() or anything under fplai/backtest/ -- both are outside this task's owned paths and fixing them changes Phase-1-gate-adjacent behaviour I was not authorised to touch. Recommend either a store.py fix (explicit ORDER BY on observations()/as_of(), same pattern) or a backtest-side fix (sort candidates before build_squad, mirroring RandomBaseline's own existing defensive comment) as a follow-on story; the Phase 1 'gate passed' pinned range for greedy_form in docs/HANDOFF.md is not actually stable and should be re-verified or re-stated as a range once fixed.

detail: Fixed the time-bomb the architect flagged: fplai.sampling.already_sampled_entry_ids's now_fn parameter was declared but its body called datetime.now(timezone.utc) directly, ignoring it. Wired the body to use now_fn(); updated tests/test_sampling.py's three failing tests to inject a FIXED far-future now_fn instead of relying on literal fixture dates being in the past relative to the real clock. Immediately made the SAME class of mistake once more while writing tests/test_sample_picks.py (a literal PAST_DEADLINE date string that was still in the future relative to real now) -- caught it myself via the identical failure signature before it reached the report, fixed by computing PAST_DEADLINE from datetime.now(UTC)-timedelta(days=1) at import time instead of a literal. Documented both as a standing lesson in already_sampled_entry_ids's own docstring: a fixed literal date compared against the real clock is a rule-7 violation regardless of which direction it currently evaluates.

Blocker 2 (cached 404 TTL) -- design and live confirmation. Fixed at the policy layer: ResponseCache (transport.py) gained max_age_for_404_seconds + now_fn; a cached 404 older than the TTL, OR carrying no stored cached_at at all (every 404 file written before this fix), is now a cache MISS transparently for every caller -- no force_refresh sprinkled at call sites. FPLClient's default cache enables a 1-hour TTL (client.ENTRY_404_TTL_SECONDS); other providers (HttpTransport/PL API/Odds API) are unaffected, opted out by default -- no live evidence gathered this session that their 404s are similarly temporal, so left unchanged rather than presumed. LIVE, READ-ONLY VERIFICATION against the real (unmodified) cache/fpl_api/: all 9 previously-identified poisoned entry/{id}/ 404 cache files (6250000, 7000000, 6185942, 6187500, 6185973, 8000000, 6500000, 6186034, 6186523) now report as ResponseCache misses under the fixed policy; a real cached 200 (entry/3434577/event/1/picks/) is unaffected. No cache file was modified or deleted (cache/** is read-only for this story) -- the fix neutralises them structurally, by their own missing timestamp, not by touching disk.

Blocker 1 (503 maintenance window) -- fail-first proof and live verification. Proved fail-first against the actual pre-fix code (git show HEAD:src/fplai/client.py, loaded via importlib, not reasoned about): a synthetic 503 raised FPLApiError immediately, zero retries, confirming the exact bug. Fixed: client.py's FPL_BACKOFF_TRIGGER_STATUSES adds 503 to this client's own default (BACKOFF_TRIGGER_STATUSES unchanged for other HttpTransport-based providers); _get/entry_picks gained a per-call max_retries override so a readiness probe can fail FAST (max_retries=0, no internal ~7min backoff ladder) while the main sampling loop uses a bounded retry (MAIN_LOOP_MAX_RETRIES=1) instead of the client default (3) so one flaky entry cannot cost minutes. probe_picks_endpoint_ready() (scripts/sample_picks.py) replaces the false-green readiness gate: check_ready() only verified the deadline had passed via bootstrap_static() staying up, which is NOT evidence picks/ itself is serving (verified live 21-22 Aug: the maintenance window is endpoint-scoped). Blocker 3 (picks widening + automatic_subs grain) -- decision, evidence, and a real scope constraint found along the way. automatic_subs[] is a genuinely different grain from picks[] (one row per substitution event per entry-gameweek, not per pick) -- given its own capability (schemas.MANAGER_AUTOMATIC_SUBS_GAMEWEEK) and dataset (automatic_subs), entity key (entry_id, event, element_out). COULD NOT be verified by uniqueness against a real POPULATED batch this session -- GW1 had not finished scoring at any point this session; automatic_subs was [] in all 11 real payloads sampled (both s002's earlier probes and this session's own live dry-run). The design instead rests on the FPL API's publicly documented field names (entry/element_in/element_out/event), flagged explicitly as unverified in the schema description, WITH a runtime substitute: scripts/sample_picks.py's _assert_automatic_subs_key_uniqueness enforces the declared key on every real batch the script ever collects going forward, logging loudly and dropping (never silently accepting) a violating chunk without touching the picks capture alongside it. Widened _picks_to_rows at zero marginal cost (element_type; entry_history's event/points/total_points/rank/rank_sort/percentile_rank/overall_rank_percentage). SCOPE CONSTRAINT FOUND: fplai.providers.fpl.py has its OWN separate, narrower _picks_to_rows/_fetch_picks implementation (not used live by sample_picks.py, but validated by tests/test_provider_fpl.py) that is OUTSIDE this story's owned paths. Only promoted overall_rank to schemas.py's required_fields (already produced by both implementations); the other widened fields are documented as present-but-optional rather than required, specifically so as not to break providers/fpl.py's own validate() call, which I am not authorised to update in step. Flagged in the schema description as a finding for the Architect: two implementations of one capability that can silently drift in column coverage is itself worth attention.

Incremental persistence against the append-only, batch-stamped store -- design note. BitemporalStore.write() stamps ONE valid_at/observed_at pair per call across the whole batch (read-only for this story, not changed). The honest resolution is a CHUNK, not a single end-of-run write (pre-fix; a single 503 anywhere in ~83 min discarded everything) and not one write per entry either (would spend a whole batch-write and a distinct observed_at on every single request -- noise, not honesty, for entries a few seconds apart). scripts/sample_picks.py now accumulates CHUNK_SIZE (default 500, ~4 min of requests) entries worth of rows, then issues ONE store.write() call per chunk stamped with THAT chunk's own real completion time as observed_at -- valid_at stays constant at the gameweek deadline across every chunk (a genuine, non-fabricated domain fact: picks are locked in AT the deadline, time-invariant across the whole collection window). Resumability (fplai.sampling.already_sampled_entry_ids, new) lets a re-invocation with the same (event, seed) -- a fully deterministic draw -- skip entries already persisted from a prior/crashed run; a genuine 404 miss is indistinguishable from never attempted and is re-requested on resume (documented trade-off, correctness-safe, costs some redundant requests, never risks silently skipping a now-real entry). Found and fixed during test-writing, not spec'd upfront: the warm-up probe (probe_picks_available) draws from the SAME entry_ids list the main loop uses, so it had to be reordered to run AFTER resume-filtering rather than before -- otherwise a resumed run would re-issue live requests for already-persisted entries just to run the probe, quietly defeating part of the point of resuming. Calibration (the mandatory selected_by_percent check) reads back the FULL persisted sample from the store at the end of run(), not just the current invocation's in-memory rows -- required for correctness after a resume, where a prior crashed run's chunks are on disk but not in this process's memory.

ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT ERROR, self-caught, worth recording because it nearly produced a false bug report. I tested check_heartbeat.py exit codes as: python script.py | tail -6; echo exit=$?.
